title: Torres del Paine: Chilean Patagonia's great park
meta_description: Torres del Paine guide: W and O treks, viewpoints, wildlife, how to get there from Puerto Natales or El Calafate and where to stay.
hero_subtitle: Granite towers, turquoise lakes and glaciers in southern Chile.
photo_alt: Lake and mountains in Torres del Paine

why_visit.title: The Paine massif
why_visit.text: The Towers and the Horns of Paine form one of the world's most famous mountain landscapes.

why_visit.title: Trekking
why_visit.text: The W and O circuits are among South America's most sought-after treks.

why_visit.title: Wildlife
why_visit.text: Guanacos, rheas, condors and one of the best chances to see wild pumas.

activities.title: Base of the Towers viewpoint
activities.text: A long, demanding hike ending in front of the three granite towers. It can be done as a day hike.

activities.title: W Trek
activities.text: Several days through the park's best-known valleys. Requires confirmed bookings at refugios or campsites.

activities.title: Lake Grey
activities.text: A lake with icebergs and the front of Grey Glacier, reached by boat trips in season.

activities.title: Viewpoints by car
activities.text: Salto Grande, the Cuernos viewpoint and Lake Pehoé can be visited on short walks from the road.

activities.title: Puma tracking
activities.text: Specialized tours with trackers greatly improve the odds of seeing one.

how_to_get_there:
From Chile: fly to Punta Arenas (PUQ) and take a bus to Puerto Natales, the base town, and from there to the park.

From Argentina: most travelers combine it with El Calafate, crossing overland to Puerto Natales.

To the park: there are buses from Puerto Natales, day tours and rental cars. There's an entrance fee, best arranged before your trip.

where_to_stay.budget: Campsites inside the park, booked in advance, and guesthouses in Puerto Natales.
where_to_stay.midrange: Refugios on the trek and hotels in Puerto Natales, the usual choice for day trips.
where_to_stay.luxury: Hotels and lodges inside the park, many with full board and excursions included.

practical_tips.title: Border and bookings
practical_tips.text: If you come from Argentina, carry valid documents. You need confirmed bookings to sleep inside the park.

practical_tips.title: Changeable weather
practical_tips.text: Wind and sudden weather changes are part of the trip. Dress in layers and always carry a windbreaker.

practical_tips.title: Book ahead
practical_tips.text: In high season, lodging and tours fill up. It's best to book as soon as you have your dates.

practical_tips.title: Prices and payments
practical_tips.text: Prices change often: check current rates before you travel and carry some cash as well as cards.

closing: Even with a single day, Torres del Paine is worth the trip. If you can, stay longer and explore it on foot.
